name: What's the difference between a guest suite and an Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU)?

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between a guest suite and an Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU)?

acceptedAnswer.text: While often used interchangeably, a key difference between a guest suite and an ADU lies in their legal definition and intended use. A guest suite is typically considered part of the main dwelling, primarily for temporary guests, and may share utilities or have limited independent functionality. An ADU, however, is a separate, complete living unit with its own kitchen, bathroom, sleeping area, and often a separate entrance, designed for long-term occupancy or rental, and must meet specific zoning and building codes for independent dwellings. ADUs have more stringent requirements than simple guest suites.
acceptedAnswer.description: A guest suite is part of the main home for temporary guests, while an ADU is a legally separate, self-contained living unit with full amenities for independent, long-term occupancy.
